title: Register Bounds Imply the Configuration Guard
statement: Let $x$ be a Boolean input word, $B$ a natural number, $	ext{st}$ a machine state whose seven registers are all at most $B$, and $l$ an instruction label. The configuration with label $l$, register values given by $	ext{st}$, and no answer satisfies the machine guard: any register-equality instruction compares distinct registers; input-comparison instructions are used only on inputs of the required valid plain or paired form; and an oracle call has no repeated register arguments. Its register values are all at most $B$.
hypotheses_covered: Every register of st is at most B.
replaced:
For any register state $\mathrm{st}$ whose seven register values are at most $B$, any
input bit string $x$, and any instruction label $l$, the configuration with label $l$,
register values given by $\mathrm{st}$, and no answer satisfies the machine's
preconditions and has every register value at most $B$.
